_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x22-rb-input.json and opened no other file, repository search, web page or API.

hints.reason: Airstrip/landing strip for AIRPORT and comic strip for COMIC are both instantly familiar senses of strip.

pairs.pair_note: Clean, familiar double meaning.

hints.reason: "The Ants Go Marching" brings ANT and March the month brings MONTH; the song gives a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the children's song is near-universal in the U.S.

hints.reason: Running a bar tab for BAR and the Tab key for KEYBOARD are two everyday, distinct senses.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent tight double meaning.

hints.reason: Baby Moses in the basket among the reeds gives BASKET and Moses raising his staff (rod) at the Red Sea gives STAFF; both are iconic Bible images.

pairs.pair_note: Satisfying indirect-knowledge hint; text is accurate.

hints.reason: A champion's title belt gives BELT and a book's title gives BOOK; fair and clear.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; the BOOK side is broad (many things have titles) but the BELT side pins the pair.

hints.reason: Coal-black colour gives BLACK and the coal mine gives MINE; plain but both sides are immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, obvious clue; fine as an easy pair.

hints.reason: Bodyboard for BODY and surfboard for SURFING are instantly familiar compounds that also share a beach scene.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but the shared beach context makes it cohesive rather than arbitrary.

hints.reason: "Taste the Rainbow" makes TASTE instant, but the BOWLING side relies on skittles the pin game, which is mainly British and only moderately known to U.S. players.

pairs.pair_note: Lovely aha for players who know skittles as ninepins; genuinely unsure how many U.S. players do, so a second opinion is worth having.

hints.reason: Cabbage patch gives CABBAGE and Cabbage Patch Kids gives DOLL; the toy craze makes the pairing click.

pairs.pair_note: Both routes run through the same brand name, but it is instantly familiar and satisfying.

hints.reason: Gin rummy gives CARD and the cotton gin (a school-history staple) gives COTTON; two unrelated senses with a nice click.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: Cats scratch for CAT and scratch-off lottery tickets for TICKET; both familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: The restaurant bill is the CHECK and the platypus's duck-like bill gives PLATYPUS; the synonym side is paired with a vivid second sense.

pairs.pair_note: Synonym of CHECK, but the platypus side makes it a real double meaning.

hints.reason: A chick hatches for CHICK and a ship's or submarine's hatch is a door for DOOR; clean verb/noun double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: A talon is a bird of prey's claw (CLAW) and hawks grip prey with talons (HAWK); near-synonym but honestly links both.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and a little flat, but fair and accurate.

hints.reason: Dye changes COLOR and dyeing eggs is a classic EASTER tradition.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, pleasant clue.

hints.reason: Spaghetti is a NOODLE and Spaghetti Westerns are Italian-made COWBOY films; a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent indirect link.

hints.reason: Detectives follow clues (DETECTIVE) and crossword puzzles are solved from clues (PUZZLE); obvious but sound.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; the board game Clue reinforces both sides.

hints.reason: Dress rehearsal gives DRESS and rehearsing a play gives PLAY; the theatre context ties them together.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar phrase plus shared theatre scene; fine.

hints.reason: Chickens lay eggs (EGG) and "Why did the chicken cross the road?" gives ROAD; the joke makes it fun.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but satisfying; chicken-and-egg adds a second echo.

hints.reason: Toppling dominoes (domino effect) gives FALL and Domino sugar, a staple U.S. brand, gives SUGAR.

pairs.pair_note: Clever brand double meaning; strong.

hints.reason: Earth, Wind & Fire completes both FIRE and WIND, and the classical elements (earth, wind/air, fire) reinforce the trio.

pairs.pair_note: Band-name join, but instantly familiar and doubled by the elements; passes the phrase-join bar.

hints.reason: Mall food court gives FOOD and a court of law gives JUDGE; two distinct, everyday senses.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: Full moon and new moon are the two best-known phases, giving FULL and NEW as opposites.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join with a satisfying opposites angle; text accurate.

hints.reason: A spade is a GARDEN digging tool and spades are a card SUIT; SUIT read as card suit is a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; misdirection on SUIT (clothing) makes it satisfying.

hints.reason: Sock puppet gives SOCK instantly; glove puppet for GLOVE is less common in the U.S. (hand puppet is usual) but still clear.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant; GLOVE side slightly softer than SOCK.

hints.reason: Achilles' heel gives HEEL and its meaning, a weak spot, gives WEAK; tight and broadly known.

pairs.pair_note: Easy once seen; the idiom's meaning makes WEAK fair.

hints.reason: A pony is a small HORSE and ponytail gives TAIL; simple and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, solid.

hints.reason: Venetian gondolas give ITALY and ski-resort gondola lifts give SKI; a pleasing two-sense link.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: Night-hunting owls make OWL instant, but the KIWI side needs players to read KIWI as the bird (not the fruit) and know it is nocturnal, which is only moderately known.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate but the kiwi half is a step most players will not take unaided; no clearly better single hint comes to mind.

hints.reason: A key opens a LOCK and skeleton key gives SKELETON; familiar and coherent.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but nice: SKELETON misdirects toward bones.

hints.reason: Tolkien's Middle-earth gives MIDDLE and Earth is our PLANET; MIDDLE is a fun misdirect.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; note EARTH is also the hint for FIRE + WIND in this batch, so avoid placing both on one board.

hints.reason: "Nail in the coffin" gives NAIL and vampires sleeping in coffins gives VAMPIRE; both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Good; idiom plus horror trope.

hints.reason: Sudoku is a PUZZLE filled with the NUMBERs 1 to 9; direct and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clear clue.

hints.reason: Panning for gold gives PAN and prospectors working river gravel gives RIVER; one vivid gold-rush scene.

pairs.pair_note: Solid scene hint.

hints.reason: Wilbur the pig of Charlotte's Web gives PIG and Wilbur Wright the aviation pioneer gives PILOT; two famous Wilburs.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent name double; one of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: Parrot-on-the-shoulder makes PIRATE instant, but SILVER only arrives via Long John Silver's parrot Captain Flint, and both routes funnel through the pirate idea, so the SILVER side is a second step many players will not take.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are correct; the issue is that SILVER is reached only through a specific character detail.

hints.reason: Diving into a POOL and skydiving from the SKY; both familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair.

hints.reason: Beaker the Muppet gives PUPPET and lab beakers give SCIENCE; a fun, fair aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; Beaker is himself a lab assistant, so the two senses echo nicely.

hints.reason: Snap, Crackle and Pop of Rice Krispies give RICE and the regional word pop gives SODA.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent cereal-mascot aha.

hints.reason: A safecracker gives SAFE and crackers crumbled into soup give SOUP; unrelated senses that click.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: A boot is footwear like a SHOE and the British boot is a car's TRUNK, a Britishism most U.S. players know.

pairs.pair_note: The owner's own example of a familiar British term; passes.

hints.reason: The Empire State gives STATE and The Empire Strikes Back gives STRIKE; two iconic names.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but both are instantly familiar and the Star Wars title is a fun payoff.

hints.reason: Viruses are everyday germs (VIRUS) and wheat germ is the embryo of the kernel (WHEAT); a clean double meaning.
hints.fix: A virus is a kind of germ, and wheat germ is the nutrient-rich embryo of a wheat kernel.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the explanation calls wheat germ the kernel's "core", but the germ is the embryo at the base of the kernel, so the fix rewords it to match the WHEAT line.
